content.comment_body: Hello, I have [product_name] with two [product_name] modules ([article_no]). Today I discovered that one of the modules (nearest to the main unit) stopped measuring, and both inputs returned zero. After switching the device off and on, functionality was restored, but for several hours it continued heating at full power. How can I easily identify this type of hardware failure and implement self-recovery without turning off the device? I appreciate any advice.

Hello [user_name], If an analog input module freezes, it may be due to interference from the sensor or the power supply. For programming, you can monitor input values with a threshold switch for zero readings, which activates an alarm after a set period and switches the heating to safety mode. A hardware reset cannot be performed via software, but you could configure an output to control an external relay with a delay, temporarily disconnecting the unit from power. Kind regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], thanks for your response. This month, we've encountered two issues with [product_name], both following extended power outages. Prior to this, the system ran for months without failures, even with occasional power drops. The first issue involved changing a WM parameter right after power was restored, which happened during the next data logging cycle. The second issue began three hours after power recovery. I've now added a threshold under 50 for all four sensors (two controlling, two for additional monitoring), and will rewire the sensors so each control sensor connects to its own module. Thanks and best regards, [user_name]

Sudden restoration of the power grid is risky for electronic devices due to voltage surges, which can cause damage. I once lost an audio amplifier to a similar event. If your [product_name] operates on 230V and the issue persists, the device may be damaged.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering sporadic hardware malfunctions with [product_name] modules, particularly after power interruptions. Analog input modules may cease reporting values and require a manual restart. There is concern over equipment running unsafely for extended periods and a lack of robust detection or automatic recovery strategies.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to reliably identify hardware issues, receive automated notifications when modules fail, and have built-in mechanisms for recovery or safe fallback that do not require manual power cycling.
